newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to ask IMF to extend stand-by program.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to ask IMF to extend stand-by program.

text.p: The Venezuelan government has decided to ask the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for an extension to its current one year stand-by program until at least December 1997, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
Venezuela signed the stand-by agreement with the IMF on July 12 last year.

"We haven't fixed a date yet, that depends on our discussions with the IMF. But we have decided to extend the agreement until at least December of this year," Matos told reporters before meeting with the Congressional finance commission.

Matos said the government had decided against asking for an IMF extended facility, which can last up to three years, "as that would move into the period of the next government." Elections are due in December 1998.
"But we have agreed to go for an extension of the stand-by program," he said.
Matos said he would be meet next week with IMF head Michel Camdessus to make the proposal "in view of the positive results we have achieved in the program currently under execution."
